headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: browser/MCP-enabled diagram agent can feed untrusted content into a broad-egress RAG agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents and HTML/MHTML, while next-ai-draw-io can use browsers and MCP, so untrusted content can plausibly bridge into instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation, but the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced. Both agents expose file-based inputs, making prompt injection plausible in default use.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io imports or summarizes attacker-controlled web or diagram content into prompts, THEN kotaemon may receive instruction-like text.
IF either agent treats file contents as trusted instructions, THEN injected directives can propagate across the pair.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompting from imported files.
Require provenance labels on all imported content.
Use a separate workspace for untrusted documents.
Strip hidden text/comments from PDFs, HTML, and diagram XML.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-boundary checks.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and handle sensitive classes: kotaemon explicitly touches API keys and chat transcripts, while next-ai-draw-io handles documents and images. If they share a workspace or the diagram agent forwards file contents to third-party APIs, sensitive material can leak. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, THEN documents and keys can be exposed across tools.
IF next-ai-draw-io sends imported file contents to external model APIs, THEN sensitive document content can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces per agent.
Remove secrets from shared folders.
Route both agents to local-only models for sensitive jobs.
Review outbound API destinations before use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad egress, and both can operate on files in overlapping workflows. kotaemon writes to ./ktem_app_data, while next-ai-draw-io edits diagrams and files; if co-located, concurrent writes can conflict. No locking or coordination is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write into the same directory, THEN file clobbering or stale reads can occur.
IF either agent modifies shared diagram or document state without locks, THEN concurrent edits can conflict.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize edits to shared files.
Use version control for shared artifacts.
Take a quick backup before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io uses natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, and kotaemon is a RAG/chat agent that can consume generated text and citations. That creates a default pathway where one agent's output can become the other's input without verification, enabling compounding hallucinations or incorrect actions. Because the pair lacks documented validation gates, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io generates a diagram or summary that kotaemon later answers from, THEN errors can cascade into downstream outputs.
IF kotaemon republishes unverified citations from imported content, THEN next-ai-draw-io may visualize false claims.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of generated outputs.
Mark AI-generated artifacts as untrusted by default.
Cross-check citations against source files.
Limit downstream actions to read-only previews.
requires-engineering: add verification and provenance propagation.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and chat transcripts, while next-ai-draw-io handles documents and images and can call multiple external model providers. If regulated or confidential documents are processed, differing retention and residency policies across those providers can create compliance gaps. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed through external model APIs, THEN retention/residency obligations may be violated.
IF API keys or chat transcripts are stored alongside documents, THEN retention controls must cover multiple data classes.
mitigations: Restrict use to non-sensitive documents.
Choose providers with matching retention terms.
Delete temporary uploads after each session.
Separate secrets from document workspaces.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
